messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to perform a statistical t-test on two independent data sets with significance levels alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01.

We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35]
Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36]

They want two tests at alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01.

We'll use the tool "functions.t_test". Provide dataset_A, dataset_B, alpha as needed. We need to call twice? The tool likely returns result; we can provide both results separately or combine them into one output. Probably best to run once per alpha. But maybe we can pass alpha param each time. We'll produce two calls.

Let's compute manually first approximate values:

Compute mean of A:
Sum A: 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: (12+15)=27, +18=45, +20=65, +22=87, +25=112, +28=140, +30=170, +32=202, +35=237. So mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Mean of B:
Sum B: 14+17=31, +19=50, +21=71, +23=94, +26=120, +29=149, +31=180, +33=213, +36=249. Mean_B = 24.9.

Difference in means: -1.2 (i.e., B higher).

Now variances: For sample variance s^2 = Σ(x_i - x̄)^2 / (n-1). Compute quickly.

For A deviations from 23.7:
12 -> diff=-11.7 squared=136.89
15->diff=-8.7 sq=75.69
18->-5.7 sq=32.49
20->-3.7 sq=13.69
22->-1.7 sq=2.89
25->1.3 sq=1.69
28->4.3 sq=18.49
30->6.3 sq=39.69
32->8.3 sq=68.89
35->11.3 sq=127.69

Sum squares: Let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58; +32.49=245.07; +13.69=258.76; +2.89=261.65; +1.69=263.34; +18.49=281.83; +39.69=321.52; +68.89=390.41; +127.69=518.10 approx.

So s_A^2 = 518.10/(10-1) = 57.566... Actually 518.10/9 ≈ 57.567.

s_A = sqrt(57.567) ~ 7.586.

Similarly for B deviations from 24.9:
14 diff=-10.9 sq=118.81
17 diff=-7.9 sq=62.41
19 diff=-5.9 sq=34.81
21 diff=-3.9 sq=15.21
23 diff=-1.9 sq=3.61
26 diff=1.1 sq=1.21
29 diff=4.1 sq=16.81
31 diff=6.1 sq=37.21
33 diff=8.1 sq=65.61
36 diff=11.1 sq=123.21

Sum squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90.

s_B^2 = 478.90/9 = 53.211...

s_B = sqrt(53.211) ≈ 7.295.

Pooled standard error SE_pooled = sqrt(s_A^2/n + s_B^2/m) where n=m=10. So SE = sqrt((57.567)/10 + (53.211)/10 ) = sqrt(5.7567 + 5.3211) = sqrt(11.0778) = 3.328.

Wait that's not pooled but difference se formula: sqrt(s_A^2/n + s_B^2/m). Yes.

Thus t-statistic = (mean_A - mean_B)/SE = (-1.2)/3.328 = -0.3607.

Degrees freedom df = n+m-2 = 18.

Critical t-values: At α=0.05 two-tailed, t_crit ≈ ±2.101. At α=0.01 two-tailed, t_crit ≈ ±2.878.

Since |t|=0.361 < critical thresholds, fail to reject null hypothesis at both levels. p-value > .70 probably.

But we should rely on tool's calculation. Use function t_test with dataset arrays and alpha accordingly.
